records.supported_name_scope: Representative Piriá system identity is supported by continuous generalized source correspondence from the selected headward setting southwest of Nova Esperança do Piriá through the Cristal, Japim, BR-316 and Curupaiti corridors to São José do Piriá and the Piriá estuary west of the separate Gurupi estuary.
records.region: Northeastern Pará, Brazil; Nova Esperança do Piriá–Curupaiti–São José do Piriá–Piriá estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Two distinct original IBGE municipal maps provide overlapping coverage of all three selected FIDs. The independent original Figure 1 in Santos and Aviz (2021) confirms the Piriá estuarine configuration, separate Gurupi estuary and Atlantic receiving setting. All selected components have bounded geographic correspondence; no material source gap remains. Three original PDF acquisitions completed HTTP200. No new acquisition restriction or availability stop was observed.

naming_scope_details.actual_selected_terminal_scope: Widening inner Piriá estuarine approach, not a surveyed outer-ocean mouth.
naming_scope_details.component_scope_limits: The initial short headward feeder is not independently labelled by the read map and retains a null individual name. Rio Piriá is a representative candidate, not a scalar name for every selected vertex, feeder or tidal channel. The selected endpoint lies in the widening Piriá estuarine approach; it is not asserted to be the surveyed outer ocean mouth. Adjacent tidal branches, the Gurupi and Atlantic receiving water retain distinct scopes. Exact naming boundaries, official registry status and Korean rendering remain unverified.

records.geographic_disambiguation: The terminal is in the northern Holbæk Bugt–Danmark Fjord setting. Fyns Sø and Skjoldungeelv are adjacent, distinct source labels; Centrum Sø belongs to the middle valley setting. The southern ice/Lambert Land and Nioghalvfjerdsfjorden context must not be substituted for the actual northern ending.
records.completion_scope: The entire selected FID8834 headward ice opening, landfall, western bend, middle loop and western Centrum Sø valley crossing, northern land connector and actual Holbæk Bugt ending are covered by the retained original Sheet9 at ordinary generalized corridor scale.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The full selected route is geographically read, but it traverses distinct ice, exposed-land, Quaternary-covered valley and lake-adjacent settings before ending at Holbæk Bugt. No primary cartographic label supports a representative natural-river identity spanning this route. This is a naming-scope limitation, not missing geographic coverage.
records.region: Northeastern Greenland, western ice and Kronprins Christian Land to Holbæk Bugt, Danmark Fjord.

naming_scope_details.actual_terminal_context: Southern inner Holbæk Bugt, connected to Danmark Fjord

records.region: Eastern Venezuela, Imataca/Delta Amacuro southern tributaries and the Arature–Río Grande internal Orinoco delta setting.
records.material_pending_reason: Two material FID10854 transitions remain unresolved in the available original hydrographic linework: the Surumo-to-Santa María corridor and the Cuyubini/El Terror-to-Guayocaicara connector. Broader maps do not settle those branch relationships.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The lower selected route, including FID 10855, corresponds to Caño Arature, called Río Arature on the Fundación Empresas Polar regional sheet. It enters the Río Grande branch of the Orinoco upstream of the open Atlantic. Original CVG geological maps place upper FID 10854 among separately labeled Surumo, Santa María, Cuyubini and Guayocaicara corridors. Two material upper/middle transitions remain indistinct in the available hydrographic linework; the broader state and delta maps do not settle them. The record is material-pending, not a completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.completion_scope: Lower Arature across FIDs10854/10855 and the actual Río Grande receiver are supported; upper named settings are observed, but two material FID10854 connectors remain source-material pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Caño Arature, called Río Arature on the regional sheet, is supported only for the selected lower delta reach and its entry into Río Grande. A full representative-system identity is not completed.

naming_scope_details.unresolved_source_name_discrepancy: CVG upper sheet reads Santa María; SAGECAN/Fundación Empresas Polar use Santa Marta in the corresponding broad setting. Variant-name equivalence is unestablished.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Internal delta receiving channel upstream of the open Atlantic; retained sea class is model metadata.
component_scope_limits: Caño Arature is supported for the selected lower delta reach. That finding does not rename all upper tributaries or establish a uniform hydronym for the complete model line.

Río Surumo, Río Santa María, Río Cuyubini and Río Guayocaicara are preserved as separate source labels. Their presence and regional association do not, by themselves, establish the selected connecting passages.

The CVG NB-20-4 original reads Río Santa María. The SAGECAN Bolívar map and Fundación Empresas Polar regional depiction use Santa Marta in the corresponding broad southern delta setting. These readings are retained as a source-level discrepancy; a formal variant-name equivalence is not established.
Río Acure, Río Ibaruma, Brazo Imataca, Caño Basama, Río Amacuro and Río Barima are separate neighboring waterways. None is assigned as a synonym for the complete selected route.

The geological maps' alluvial unit polygons are geological coverage, not evidence of a selected lake or reservoir passage. No material named lake or reservoir passage was identified on the selected route.

A channel can be intermittent and still supply geographic correspondence. The unresolved issue is the connecting channel relationship, not a requirement for continuous perennial flow or exact vertex agreement.

records.region: Central Pacific Andes of Peru; Ticllacocha–Tanta–Nor Yauyos–Cañete valley to Herbay Bajo.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Inspected original MTC cartography follows the selected Ticllacocha–Tanta headwater, Paucarcocha connection, eastward bend to Vilca, southward Nor Yauyos corridor, middle valley and lower Cañete to the actual Pacific coast. An original PROMPERÚ map distinguishes Papacocha, Hualhua and Piquecocha along the upper valley, while the primary 2018 hydrological study distinguishes Paucarcocha, Capillucas and El Platanal's restitution setting. The combined evidence supports Río Cañete as representative system identity without renaming the lake passages or lateral tributaries.
records.completion_scope: Inspected original MTC cartography follows the selected Ticllacocha–Tanta headwater, Paucarcocha connection, eastward bend to Vilca, southward Nor Yauyos corridor, middle valley and lower Cañete to the actual Pacific coast. An original PROMPERÚ map distinguishes Papacocha, Hualhua and Piquecocha along the upper valley, while the primary 2018 hydrological study distinguishes Paucarcocha, Capillucas and El Platanal's restitution setting. The combined evidence supports Río Cañete as representative system identity without renaming the lake passages or lateral tributaries.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative river-system identity for the selected headwater-to-Pacific corridor, not a uniform scalar name for lakes, tributaries, reservoir water or every headward segment

naming_scope_details.hydroelectric_context: El Platanal diversion and restitution are context; selected river valley is not replaced by the diversion.
naming_scope_details.actual_receiving_waterbody: Pacific Ocean by Herbay Bajo / Boca del Río
component_scope_limits: The representative candidate is Río Cañete. A name covering every part of the selected lake-and-river route as one uniform scalar feature is not asserted.

Laguna Ticllacocha, Laguna Paucarcocha, Laguna Papacocha, Hualhua/Huallhua and Laguna Piquecocha retain their distinct lake roles. The PROMPERÚ map prints Hualhua; the regional tourism inventory prints Huallhua. This is recorded source spelling, not a registry adjudication.

The selected southern Ticllacocha approach is distinguished from the northern and northwestern lake-fed tributaries near Paucarcocha. Piscococha and Chuspicocha are lateral lake settings, not all selected passages.
Alis, Laraos, Huantán, Tupe, Cacra and other lateral drainage are junction context; they are not renamed Cañete by this representative identity.

The name of the first short selected headward segment, taken independently of the named lake and representative river system, remains null. No Korean name or formal registry status has been established.
Correspondence is at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale. No exact bank, vertex, modern reservoir shoreline, perennial-flow, diversion-operation or mouth-point claim is made.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
